cohort: The study included all 238 children born at a single tertiary medical center between 2011 and 2017 who did not pass the Universal Newborn Hearing Screening (UNHS) and were subsequently diagnosed with hearing impairment (HI).
finding: Children from consanguineous marriage cultural backgrounds diagnosed with HI demonstrated lower rates of cochlear implantation compliance, performed at a significantly older age, and had significantly lower bilateral CI compliance compared to controls.
followup_time: Up to 36.5 months post-birth (age at CI for some children)
